summary: City of Madison allows up to 8 chickens with a city chicken license on lots with up to four dwelling units. Roosters and on-site slaughter are prohibited.
chickenLimit: Up to 8 chickens
permitRequired: City chicken license required ($10 by mail per the city page)
prerequisites: Apply within 30 days of getting chickens and renew before January 1 each year (license year runs January 1 to December 31).
Complete required notifications when you rent, live in a two- to four-unit building, or keep chickens at a museum, school, or day care. Owner-occupied single-family homes do not need to notify.
Register with the Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration program (free) before submitting the city license application.
rules: Chickens must have a covered enclosure and stay in the covered or fenced enclosure at all times.
The enclosure must be at least 25 feet from any residential structure on an adjacent lot.
Keeping chickens is allowed as an accessory use on lots with up to four dwelling units, and at museums, schools, or day care centers.

Coop and yard together must provide at least 16 square feet per chicken.
Coops cannot be taller than 10 feet or exceed 50 square feet, and must be raised or on a hard surface.
Enclosures must be at least 25 feet from any residential structure on an adjacent lot and cannot be in the front yard.

summary: City of Appleton allows up to 6 hens on single-family or two-family properties with an annual Health Department permit and a pre-license inspection. Roosters are not allowed.
chickenLimit: Up to 6 chickens (hens only)
roosterRule: Roosters not allowed (the rules define chickens as hens only)
permitRequired: Annual Health Department permit; the 2026 application lists an $81 pre-inspection fee and a $28 annual license
prerequisites: Read the city's Chicken Keeping Rules and Regulations.
Register your premises with the Wisconsin Livestock Identification Consortium (free).
Submit the application with a diagram of the coop location and distances to neighboring structures, a coop design and materials plan, and a manure disposal plan.
Schedule the pre-licensing inspection. Renters need written permission from the property owner.
rules: Single-family or two-family dwellings only; not commercial or mixed-use properties.

Coop must be in the rear yard, at least 3 feet from side and rear lot lines, 10 feet from other structures on the parcel unless attached to a garage or shed, and 25 feet from a home, church, school, or business on an abutting lot.
Coop floor must give at least 2 square feet per bird, be a hard cleanable surface (no dirt floor), and the coop cannot be taller than 8 feet. The attached run is limited to 100 square feet.
Chickens must stay in the coop or attached run at all times. Off-site sale of eggs is prohibited.
Coops of 50 square feet or more need a building permit; electricity needs an electrical permit.
Unusual illness or death must be reported to the Health Department immediately.

permitRequired: Annual poultry license (January 1 to December 31) plus inspection

The city notifies owners within 100 feet; abutting owners have 14 days to object, which sends the application to the City Council.
The completed coop is inspected before the license is issued.
rules: Allowed on lots zoned R-1 and used as a single-family home, or R-2 multi-family with written support from the landlord and all tenants.
Coop and run must be in the back or side yard: at least 10 feet from an abutting lot, 25 feet from homes on adjacent lots, 5 feet from homes on your own lot, and 2 feet from all lot lines.
Detached, stationary coop only; no more than 64 square feet and 8 feet tall; at least 3 square feet per bird; hard, rodent-resistant floor.
Birds must stay in the coop or enclosed run, and be secured in the coop during non-daylight hours.
No commercial sales. Limited on-site slaughter is allowed under specific conditions in the ordinance.

Chickens need a covered enclosure of at least 3 square feet per bird and must stay in it or a fenced backyard enclosure at all times.
No enclosure may be closer than 25 feet to any home on an adjacent lot.

Renters must include a written statement of support from the property owner and a written agreement on coop maintenance and what happens to the hens if you move.

Permits run January 1 to December 31 and must be renewed each year.

summary: City of Kenosha allows up to 4 chickens on single-family properties with an annual backyard chicken coop license reviewed by a city committee. Roosters and slaughter are prohibited.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 chickens
permitRequired: Annual license; the application (rev. 10/25) lists $200 per year new and $100 per year renewal
prerequisites: Property must be zoned single-family residential; renters need the landlord's signed consent.
Attach a diagram showing property lines, the enclosure, and all structures within 100 feet.
Apply for the Wisconsin livestock premises registry; the license will not be issued until registration is verified.
List owners and adult tenants of all directly or diagonally abutting properties, including across an alley.
The application goes to the Public Safety and Welfare Committee; contact your alderperson at least 7 days before review.
rules: Coops must be in the rear yard and at least 25 feet from any home on an adjacent lot.
Provide at least 16 square feet of floor space per chicken, with at least 3 square feet per chicken under a watertight cover. Maximum coop height is 6 feet.
Coops over 120 square feet need a building permit; electricity needs an electrical permit and cannot be supplied by extension cords.
No selling chickens, eggs, or manure from the property; no commercial breeding.
Chickens stay in the coop or enclosure and may not trespass on neighboring properties. Unwanted chickens cannot be released or taken to Animal Control.

summary: City of Janesville allows up to 4 female chickens or ducks (not both) on a lot with one single-family home, with an annual residential premises permit. Roosters and drakes are not allowed.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 hens or 4 female ducks (not both)
permitRequired: Annual residential chicken or duck premises permit (fees set by City Council)
prerequisites: Get the permit before keeping birds or building a coop or run. The permit year runs January 1 to December 31.
Submit an accurately scaled drawing of the coop and run location, distances to lot lines and the nearest neighboring home, and coop and run dimensions.
Include proof of Wisconsin DATCP premises registration.
If you do not own the property, the owner must sign the application, and the signature must be notarized.
rules: One shared coop with an attached run, entirely in the rear yard.
New coops need at least 3 square feet per chicken and cannot exceed 24 square feet; coop and run together cannot be taller than 6 feet.
Run cannot exceed 50 square feet or 1% of the rear yard, whichever is greater, and never more than 200 square feet.
Coop and run must be at least 10 feet from the rear wall of your home, 10 feet from property lines, and 18 feet from any home on adjacent property.
Birds must be in the coop from sunset to sunrise. Food scraps may only be fed inside the coop. Slaughter only at a licensed facility.
Report any unusual illness or death to Wisconsin DATCP within 24 hours.

roosterRule: Roosters prohibited (ducks, geese, turkeys, and other fowl also prohibited)

prerequisites: Register the premises with the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection (DATCP) under Wis. Admin. Code ATCP 17.02 before a permit is issued.
Submit enclosure plans and a site plan showing distances to property boundaries, structures on the premises, and structures on adjoining properties for Community Development approval.
Renters on non-owner-occupied single-family parcels need written consent from the parcel owner; duplex or multi-family parcels are only eligible if the parcel owner occupies one of the units.
rules: Only one permit may be issued per tax parcel.
Enclosures must provide at least 16 square feet per chicken (including coop area), and coops must provide at least 3 square feet per chicken.
Enclosures must be covered with solid material or hardware cloth; chicken wire is not permitted for enclosures.
Coops and runs must be in the rear yard and set back at least 25 feet from neighboring residential structures and lot lines per Waukesha Municipal Code Section 33.07.
Premises with a permit must remain available for inspection by the Community Development Department.

summary: City of Wauwatosa allows up to 4 hens per residential parcel with an annual permit, site plan, and written consent from all adjoining and diagonally abutting property owners. Roosters and slaughter are prohibited.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 chickens (hens)
permitRequired: Annual chicken-keeping permit required ($50 initial fee, $20 annual renewal per city page)
prerequisites: Obtain a city permit from the Development Department before acquiring any live chickens (one permit per residential parcel).
Obtain written consent from the property owner (if renting) and from the owners of all adjoining or diagonally abutting properties, including across an alley.
Submit a site plan showing coop and enclosure dimensions and distances to lot lines and neighboring dwellings.
Register the premises with the Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration program.
rules: Chickens must be kept in a sanitary, covered coop or fenced enclosure at all times; coops and yards together must provide at least 16 square feet per chicken.
Coops must be moisture-resistant and either raised off the ground or placed on a hard surface such as concrete, patio block, or gravel.
No coop or enclosure may be in the front yard or closer than 25 feet to any residential dwelling on an adjacent lot unless that neighbor gives written consent.
Coops and yards must be cleaned of droppings, uneaten feed, feathers, and waste daily.
On-site slaughtering is prohibited, and eggs may not be sold, traded, or hatched for commercial purposes.
Unusual illness or death of chickens must be reported immediately to the Health Department.

summary: City of Fond du Lac allows up to 4 hens on owner-occupied single-family residential lots that do not already have a shed or gazebo, with an annual $50 permit. Roosters and slaughter are prohibited.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 hens and/or pullets
permitRequired: Annual Chicken Keeping Permit ($50/year; $25 late fee if renewed after March 31)
prerequisites: Applicant must be the primary owner of record and reside at the single-family residence (provide current tax bill as proof of ownership).
Register with Wisconsin DATCP (Wis. Stat. 95.51) and include proof of premises registration.
Submit a scaled site plan approved by Inspection, Fire, and Community Development, plus a drawing or photo of the henhouse showing materials and colors.
Property cannot already have an existing storage shed, gazebo, or similar accessory building (properties are limited to a garage plus one accessory structure).
rules: Chickens must be housed in a detached, stationary, rodent-resistant, insulated, and ventilated henhouse used exclusively for hens; chicken tractors and moveable structures are prohibited.
Maximum henhouse size is 12 square feet, maximum attached covered run size is 12 square feet, and maximum height is 8 feet.
Henhouse and outdoor run must be at least 15 feet from side and rear lot lines and at least 15 feet from habitable structures on adjoining properties.
Chickens must stay inside the henhouse or enclosed run at all times and be secured inside the henhouse during non-daylight hours.
On-site slaughter and commercial use (including selling eggs or fertilizer) are prohibited.

permitRequired: Annual Chicken Keeping Permit ($35/year; license year runs July 1 to June 30)

Register with Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration and submit a copy with the application to the City Clerk.

Coop and attached contiguous run must be in the rear yard, at least 10 feet from any property line and at least 25 feet from any principal residential structure on an adjacent lot.

Chickens must stay in the coop or run at all times and be secured inside the coop from sunset to sunrise.
On-site slaughter and commercial activity (including selling eggs or fertilizer) are prohibited. Feed must be stored in rodent-proof containers.

summary: City of Sun Prairie allows up to 4 hens on single-family residential lots with a one-time Special Use Permit ($35) from Planning and an annual Chicken-Keeping License ($15 renewal) from the City Clerk. Roosters are prohibited.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 hens (up to 15 hens at permitted schools)
permitRequired: One-time Special Use Permit ($35) plus annual Chicken-Keeping License (free first year with SUP, $15/year renewal due Dec. 31)
prerequisites: Register the premises with the Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration program (free) and save your registration card.
Apply for and obtain a Special Use Permit ($35) from the Planning Department with a scaled site plan and coop/enclosure elevation plan before building the coop.
After Special Use Permit approval, apply online through OpenGov for the City Clerk Chicken-Keeping License.
rules: Allowed on single-family residential lots with a single dwelling unit (and at schools under a Conditional Use Permit).
Covered coop and fenced enclosure must be in the rear yard, set back at least 15 feet from all property lines, and placed on a paved surface or raised at least 24 inches off the ground.

Combined coop and enclosure area must provide at least 16 square feet per chicken and not exceed 120 square feet total; the coop structure itself cannot exceed 50 square feet or 12 feet in height (coops over 80 sq ft total require a building permit).
Chickens may range in the rear yard outside the enclosure only if the entire rear yard is enclosed by a 6-foot-high fence and hens are returned to the coop nightly.
Feed must be stored outside the coop/enclosure in rodent-proof containers, waste must be bagged and placed in city refuse carts, and on-site slaughtering is prohibited.

summary: City of Beloit allows up to 4 female chickens on single-family residential lots with an annual residential chicken permit. Roosters and on-site slaughter are prohibited.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 female chickens
permitRequired: Annual residential chicken permit required (January 1 to December 31; fee set by City Council resolution)
prerequisites: Obtain an annual residential chicken permit from Planning and Building Services before acquiring chickens or building a coop or run.
Include proof of Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration (Wis. Stat. 95.51 and ATCP 17).
Submit an accurately scaled drawing showing coop and run dimensions and distances to lot lines and the nearest adjoining principal structure.
If the applicant is not the parcel owner, the property owner must sign the application and have the signature notarized.
rules: Allowed on residential zoning lots containing one single-family dwelling unit (Beloit Code of General Ordinances Sec. 7.244).

Coop and run must be in the rear yard, at least 10 feet from the rear wall of your home, at least 20 feet from any principal structure on adjacent property, and at least 10 feet from lot lines (or 3 feet where contiguous to an alley).
Newly built or installed coops cannot exceed 24 square feet; attached runs cannot exceed 40 square feet or 1% of the rear yard, up to a maximum of 100 square feet.
Chickens must stay in the coop or run at all times and be secured inside the coop from sunset to sunrise.
Human food scraps may only be fed inside the coop (never in the run), all feed must be in rodent-proof containers, and slaughter is prohibited except at a licensed meat processing facility.

summary: City of De Pere allows up to 4 hens on R-1 and R-2 residential parcels with an annual permit from the Clerk-Treasurer. Roosters, on-site slaughter, and egg sales are prohibited.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 chickens (combined dogs, cats, and chickens cannot exceed 6 animals)
permitRequired: Annual chicken permit from the Clerk-Treasurer (valid Jan. 1 to Dec. 31; fee matches spayed/neutered dog/cat fee)
prerequisites: Register the proposed location with Wisconsin DATCP (Wis. Stat. 95.51) and include proof with your application.
Renters must include written consent from the record title owner of the property.
Apply online or through the Clerk-Treasurer's office before keeping chickens.
rules: One permit allowed per R-1 Single-Family or R-2 Single- and Two-Family residential parcel (De Pere Municipal Code Sec. 86-5).
Keeping chickens reduces the 4-dog/cat limit so that the total number of dogs, cats, and chickens does not exceed 6 animals (and never more than 4 chickens).
Coops must provide at least 4 square feet per chicken, be moisture-resistant, and be raised off the ground or placed on concrete, patio block, or gravel; attached runs cannot exceed 40 square feet.
Coops must be in the rear yard, outside all required setbacks, and at least 25 feet from any principal residential structure on an adjacent lot.
Chickens must stay in the coop or attached run at all times (no free-ranging). On-site slaughter and selling eggs or chicks are prohibited.

Attend an approved fowl education course.
Get zoning approval from the Community Planning and Economic Development department.
Pass an inspection by an Animal Care and Control officer.
rules: The permit covers chickens, turkeys, ducks, pigeons, and quail.
Permits renew every year.
Full rules are in Minneapolis Code of Ordinances section 63.90, Fowl.

Coops over 200 square feet or that use electricity also need a building and/or electrical permit.

summary: City of Chicago allows backyard laying hens without a numeric flock cap or residential chicken permit, but strictly prohibits keeping or slaughtering any animal for meat and enforces strict sanitation, rodent-control, and noise rules.
chickenLimit: No numeric limit in city code for egg-laying hens (must meet sanitation, noise, and space standards)
roosterRule: Not explicitly banned by species, but crowing that disturbs neighbors violates Chicago noise and animal nuisance ordinances
permitRequired: No residential permit required for keeping hens for eggs (Illinois Dept. of Agriculture livestock premises registration recommended; live-poultry retail/market facilities require a license under Sec. 7-40-135)
prerequisites: Check property deed restrictions, HOA bylaws, or landlord lease terms before acquiring birds.
Confirm your coop design meets Chicago building and accessory-structure setback rules and rodent-proofing standards.
rules: Under Chicago Municipal Code Section 7-12-300, no person may own, keep, or slaughter any animal (including poultry) intended to be used for food/meat purposes; animals kept solely for eggs or milk are exempt from the possession ban, but on-site slaughtering is strictly prohibited ($50 to $1,000 fine).
Coops and enclosures must be kept clean, sanitary, and rodent-proof so they do not attract rats or create odor or noise nuisances under Chapter 7-12 and Chapter 7-28.
Birds may not run at large off the owner's premises.

Submit a site plan drawing showing coop dimensions (length x width in sq ft) and distances to your house and property lines, and pass required Health/Building inspections.

Hens must be kept in a rear-yard coop and fenced enclosure located at least 10 feet from the residence and at least 3 feet from all property lines.
Coops must be kept clean, sanitary, rodent-resistant, and free from objectionable odors.
Hen Coop Licenses expire December 31 each year and do not transfer with the land.

Coops, cages, and pens must be at least 25 feet from any dwelling or occupied structure on another parcel, at least 5 feet from all property lines, and never in a front or street-side yard.

Henhouses must provide at least 4 square feet per bird, be predator- and rodent-proof, and be located in the rear yard.

Coops and enclosures must be located in the rear yard, at least 25 feet from neighboring residential dwellings and at least 5 feet from property lines and the principal residence.
Enclosures must be predator-proof, well-ventilated, kept clean and sanitary, and provide adequate space, roosting, and nesting boxes.

roosterRule: Roosters (male chickens) prohibited; drakes (male ducks) and hen ducks are permitted

rules: Governed by Ann Arbor City Code Chapter 107 (Animals), Section 9:42 (Keeping of chickens or ducks).
Allowed on properties whose principal use is a single-family dwelling, two-family dwelling, or primary/secondary school.

Covered and fenced enclosures must be in the rear yard, at least 10 feet from any adjacent property line, and at least 40 feet from any residential structure on an adjacent lot (only the 40-foot distance can be waived with adjacent-owner consent).
Birds may be outside the enclosure in the rear or side yard only when a person is present with the birds in the same location.
Enclosures and feed storage must be constructed and maintained to prevent rats, mice, or other rodents. Slaughtering chickens or ducks is prohibited.

Upload a dimensioned site plan, coop/enclosure building plans or product spec sheet, and written landlord permission (if renting) through the Grand Rapids Citizen Access portal.
rules: Only one coop is allowed per property, located in the rear yard at least 10 feet from all property lines.
Coop cannot exceed 8 feet in height or 6 square feet per chicken, and the coop and covered run combined cannot cover more than 50% of the rear yard.
Chickens must stay confined in a clean, predator- and rodent-resistant coop and covered/fenced enclosure.
Roosters are prohibited at any age.

Supervised free-roaming in the yard is allowed up to 4 hours per day if flight is prevented (clipped wings or overhead barrier), the owner is present, and no waste leaves the property.
Up to 10 gallons of bagged waste per week may be placed in the trash, or waste may be composted on site.

summary: City of Dubuque allows chicken and duck hens for egg production on residentially zoned property with no permit and no cap on the number of hens. Roosters and drakes are prohibited.
chickenLimit: No city cap on the number of hens
permitRequired: No hen permit required; a building permit is needed only for coops with a footprint of 200 square feet or more
prerequisites: Property must be residentially zoned (not commercial).
Check coop setbacks with Planning Services (563-589-4210, planning@cityofdubuque.org) before siting your coop.
rules: Hens are allowed for egg production only.
Coops should be in the back yard and must meet accessory-structure setback requirements.
Hens must have adequate shelter and be kept in an enclosure that keeps them on your property and protects them from predators.
City nuisance and sanitary regulations apply to improper care or neighbor complaints.

summary: City of Verona allows hens with an annual chicken-keeping license. The 2026 license application lists a maximum of 4 hens and a $20 household fee, while current zoning (Article E, Sec. 13-1-132) allows up to 4 hens on lots under 1 acre and up to 8 hens on lots of 1 acre or more. Roosters and on-site slaughter are prohibited.
chickenLimit: Zoning Sec. 13-1-132 allows up to 4 female chickens on lots under 1 acre and up to 8 on lots of 1 acre or more; the City's 2026 Chicken License Application still lists a maximum of 4 hens
permitRequired: Annual chicken-keeping license required (Sec. 7-1-22). The 2026 application lists a $20 fee per household (up to 4 chickens) and a $5 late fee for licenses issued after March 31, 2026, unless the chickens are obtained after that date.
prerequisites: Obtain the annual license prior to January 1, or within 30 days of acquiring chickens. The license year is January 1 to December 31 (Sec. 7-1-22).
Provide proof of Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration before applying.
Give written notification to all property owners within 25 feet of the property and provide proof of notice to the city (not required for renewals).
If renting, obtain written permission from the property owner.
A license does not override deed restrictions, covenants, or other private limits (Sec. 7-1-22(8)).
rules: Keeping and raising of chickens is an accessory use under Zoning Ordinance Sec. 13-1-132(d) (Article E: Specific Use Standards). Source: https://www.veronawi.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3944/Article-E---Specific-Use-Standards
Chickens must have a covered coop and an enclosed run and must stay in the coop or run at all times. Source: https://www.veronawi.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3944/Article-E---Specific-Use-Standards

The coop must be in the rear yard, set back at least 15 feet from all property lines, and may not exceed 15 feet in height. It must sit on a paved surface or be raised at least 1 foot off the ground. On lots with frontage on more than one street, the coop must also be at least 25 feet from streets. Source: https://www.veronawi.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3944/Article-E---Specific-Use-Standards
A building permit is required for permanent fencing of the run. Source: https://www.veronawi.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3944/Article-E---Specific-Use-Standards

The sale of chickens, meat, eggs, or other chicken by-products is prohibited. Slaughtering of chickens is prohibited. Source: https://www.veronawi.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3944/Article-E---Specific-Use-Standards
A chicken coop and run do not count toward the maximum number of accessory structures on a lot. Source: https://www.veronawi.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3944/Article-E---Specific-Use-Standards

The license may be revoked for failure to comply; chickens must be removed within 30 days after revocation. Sources: https://www.veronawi.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2251/2026-Chicken-License-Application and https://library.municode.com/wi/verona/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=TIT7LIRE_CH1LIDOCHREAN

Official city documents disagree on the hen cap. Zoning Sec. 13-1-132 allows up to 4 female chickens on lots under 1 acre and up to 8 on lots of 1 acre or more, but the 2026 Chicken License Application still lists a maximum of 4 hens and a $20 household fee for up to 4 chickens. Confirm with the City Clerk which limit applies before getting birds. Sources: https://www.veronawi.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3944/Article-E---Specific-Use-Standards and https://www.veronawi.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2251/2026-Chicken-License-Application

summary: City of Stoughton allows up to 6 hen chickens (no roosters) on residentially zoned single-family, duplex, or twin-home lots. New keepers pay a $25 registration fee (renewals are free) and must follow zoning code Sec. 78-206(8)(y). Selling eggs and slaughtering chickens are prohibited.
chickenLimit: Up to 6 hen chickens
permitRequired: Annual registration with the City of Stoughton required (expires December 31; renew by March 31 or a $25 late fee applies). New registrations: $25. Renewals: no fee (city form updated 12-2024).
prerequisites: Register with the city before keeping chickens, and renew by March 31 each year after the December 31 expiration.
New applicants must submit a site plan showing coop/run size and distances to lot lines, plus a copy of Wisconsin livestock premises registration (WLIC).

Coops under 65 square feet are exempt from a zoning permit and fee; larger coops must meet the accessory-structure rules of the zoning district. Fencing over 100 square feet requires a zoning permit and fee.
Electrical work requires an electrical permit through Planning and Development.
rules: Allowed by right on residentially zoned property with a single-family, duplex, or twin-home unit, and for group daycares, schools, and churches in the Planned Business and Institutional zoning districts (Sec. 78-206(8)(y)). Source: https://www.cityofstoughton.com/DocumentCenter/View/633/Chicken-License-Application-PDF

The coop and run may only be in the rear yard and/or side yard and must be at least 25 feet from any residential home on an adjacent lot. Source: https://www.cityofstoughton.com/DocumentCenter/View/633/Chicken-License-Application-PDF

Chickens must stay in the coop or run at all times. Coops must provide at least 3 square feet per hen and runs at least 10 square feet per hen, plus a covered enclosure for protection. Source: https://www.cityofstoughton.com/DocumentCenter/View/633/Chicken-License-Application-PDF
Selling of eggs is prohibited. Slaughtering of chickens is prohibited. Source: https://www.cityofstoughton.com/DocumentCenter/View/633/Chicken-License-Application-PDF

Noise standards in Sec. 6-5 and noxious-odor standards in Sec. 58-8 apply. Proof of DATCP livestock premises registration must be provided upon request. Source: https://www.cityofstoughton.com/DocumentCenter/View/633/Chicken-License-Application-PDF

summary: City of Portage allows a combined total of up to 6 chickens and ducks on lots in the R1, R2, R3, and RT zoning districts with a city permit. Roosters and drakes are prohibited. The 2026 application lists a $75 initial fee and a $25 yearly renewal. Outdoor slaughter is prohibited in residential zoning districts.
chickenLimit: Up to 6 chickens and ducks combined
roosterRule: Roosters and drakes prohibited (Code 6-122, as quoted on the 2026 application)
permitRequired: City permit required. The official 2026 application (updated 2/12/2026) lists a $75 initial fee and a $25 yearly renewal fee (non-refundable, due upon filing).
prerequisites: Permits are allowed only in the R1, R2, R3, and RT zoning districts.
If the applicant is not the property owner, the owner must sign the application consenting to chickens or ducks on the property.
Attach a photo or drawing of the coop or enclosure. The coop may be part of an unattached yard shed or garage if setbacks are met, but may not be on top of a building.

If the coop/run would be closer than 15 feet to any lot line, list contiguous neighbors; the application cannot be approved if 50% or more of neighboring properties object. That neighbor section may be omitted if the coop/run is 15 feet or more from all lot lines.
rules: Rules are stated as Code 6-122 on the official 2026 application: no roosters or drakes; birds must stay in the covered coop or duck enclosure or the fenced run at all times; outdoor slaughtering of chickens or ducks in residential zoning districts is prohibited; a permit can be revoked for 3 violations within 12 months. Source: https://portagewi.gov/documents/548/Chicken_and_Duck_Application_2026.pdf

The coop, duck enclosure, or run may not be closer than 15 feet to any lot line unless neighborhood approval is received, and may not be placed in the front yard. Source: https://portagewi.gov/documents/548/Chicken_and_Duck_Application_2026.pdf

summary: Village of Waunakee allows up to 4 hens on lots in the R-1, R-2, R-3, and R-3D districts (and certain single-family PUDs) with an annual village license. Roosters are prohibited. The license fee is $15, and a $50 building permit is required for the coop. On-site slaughter is prohibited.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 chickens on residential lots (up to 15 hens at public or private educational institutions zoned G-1)
permitRequired: Annual village chicken license required ($15 for 1-4 hens, new and renewal). License year is January 1 to December 31; licenses issued after March 31 are assessed a $5 per month late fee. A $50 building permit is also required for construction of a chicken coop.
prerequisites: Obtain an HOA approval letter if an association exists, and a property-owner approval letter if the applicant is a renter.
Complete Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration and save proof.
Complete a Village zoning permit form and obtain an approved building permit ($50) for the coop before submitting the $15 chicken license application and supporting documents to the Village Clerk.
The license is non-transferable and must be renewed prior to March 31 of the following year.
rules: Allowed as an accessory use on lots in R-1, R-2, R-3, and R-3D, in a PUD designated for single-family homes unless a general development plan prohibits it, and on G-1 Institutional land for public and private educational institutions (Sec. 133-1138). Source: https://www.waunakee.gov/1136/Chicken-Licensing-Information

Chickens must have a covered coop/fenced enclosure. They may be outside the coop/enclosure if the rear yard is completely enclosed by a 6-foot fence, and they must be returned to the coop/enclosure nightly. Source: https://www.waunakee.gov/1136/Chicken-Licensing-Information

Coops/enclosures are allowed only in rear yards, must be set back at least 15 feet from all property lines and 20 feet from a dwelling on an adjacent lot, may not exceed 12 feet in height, and must sit on a paved surface or be raised at least 24 inches off the ground. Source: https://www.waunakee.gov/1136/Chicken-Licensing-Information

The combined coop and enclosure must provide at least 16 square feet per chicken and may not exceed 120 square feet; the coop structure itself may not exceed 50 square feet. Educational sites may use up to 500 square feet of combined area, with a 30-foot setback from all property lines. Source: https://www.waunakee.gov/1136/Chicken-Licensing-Information

On-site slaughter is prohibited. Feed may not be stored in the coop or enclosure and must be kept so it does not attract rodents and pests. Waste must be bagged and placed in refuse carts. Source: https://www.waunakee.gov/1136/Chicken-Licensing-Information

summary: City of Manitowoc allows up to 6 chickens with an annual license from the City Clerk. Roosters and on-site slaughter are prohibited. The municipal code sets the license tax at $10 per premises, while the city's current application packet instructs applicants to submit $15.
chickenLimit: Up to 6 chickens (MMC §11.220(4)(d); also restated on the official application)
roosterRule: Roosters, gamecocks, and other fighting birds prohibited (MMC §11.220(4)(d))
permitRequired: Annual chicken license required (MMC §11.220(4)). Code sets the license tax at $10.00 per premises, plus a $5.00 late fee if not obtained within one month of possession or by January 31 of a renewal year. The official application packet (Rev 2026) instead tells applicants to submit $15 to the City Treasurer. Licenses expire December 31.
prerequisites: Register with Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration and submit the registration number and expiration date with the city application.

Notify others as required on first application: owner-occupied single-family homes need no notification; other property types must notify the owner and residents as described in the city how-to sheet. Notification is not required for renewals.
The Chief of Police or designee verifies the property meets the enclosure and setback rules before the initial license is issued, and may inspect while the permit is in effect.
rules: No person may keep chickens or ducks without a license issued by the City Clerk (MMC §11.220(4)). Source: https://www.codepublishing.com/WI/Manitowoc/html/Manitowoc11/Manitowoc11220.html

Chickens must have a covered enclosure and must stay in the covered enclosure or a fenced enclosure at all times. The enclosure must be at least 25 feet from any residential structure on an adjacent lot. Source: https://www.codepublishing.com/WI/Manitowoc/html/Manitowoc11/Manitowoc11220.html
On-site slaughter of chickens is prohibited. Keeping more than six chickens is prohibited. Source: https://www.codepublishing.com/WI/Manitowoc/html/Manitowoc11/Manitowoc11220.html

A license may be revoked if the owner accumulates two or more violations resulting in conviction, within a 12-month period, of any ordinance regulating the keeping of chickens. Source: https://www.codepublishing.com/WI/Manitowoc/html/Manitowoc11/Manitowoc11220.html

Official city documents disagree on the license fee. MMC §11.220(4) sets the license tax at $10.00 per premises, plus a $5.00 late fee if the license is not obtained within one month of possession or by January 31 of a renewal year. The Rev 2026 application packet instead tells applicants to submit $15 to the City Treasurer. Sources: https://www.codepublishing.com/WI/Manitowoc/html/Manitowoc11/Manitowoc11220.html and https://www.manitowoc.org/DocumentCenter/View/26679/Chicken-License

summary: City of West Bend allows up to 4 chickens on single-family dwellings and duplexes in single-family or two-family zoning, with an annual $50 site license. Roosters and slaughter are prohibited. Coops and runs must generally be in the rear yard, at least 5 feet from the lot line and 25 feet from a residential or business structure on an adjacent lot.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 chickens per property (Sec. 9.075)
permitRequired: Annual site license required (Secs. 9.075 and 12.175). The official Chicken License Application lists a $50.00 per-site fee; licenses are issued for one calendar year regardless of issuance date, and a $5.00 late renewal fee applies after March 31. A building/zoning permit is also required for the coop (the city packet lists plan review, a per-square-foot building permit, and a $75 zoning permit if 100 square feet or larger).
prerequisites: Register the owner's name and address and the number of chickens and pay the license fee before keeping chickens or building a coop or run (Sec. 9.075(1)(a)).
Before a site license is issued, the City Treasurer notifies owners of adjoining and surrounding properties of the pending request.

Submit a current plat of survey showing lot lines, easements, existing buildings, and the proposed coop and fence locations to Building Inspection. Chickens are not allowed in the coop until final inspection.
It is the property owner's responsibility to confirm that deed restrictions or covenants allow chickens.
rules: Except as provided in Sec. 9.075, Sec. 9.07(1) prohibits keeping live fowl in the city, including chickens, geese, ducks, turkeys, pheasants, or guinea hens (racing or show pigeons excepted). Source: https://cms9files.revize.com/westbend/municipal%20code/09%20Chapter%20Municipal%20Code.pdf

Allowed only where the principal use is a single-family dwelling or duplex in single-family or two-family zoning (Sec. 9.075(1)(e)(1)). Source: https://cms9files.revize.com/westbend/municipal%20code/09%20Chapter%20Municipal%20Code.pdf

Chickens must stay in a waterproof, rodent-proof, and predator-proof coop in a fenced run and may not roam at large. No person shall slaughter any chickens. Source: https://cms9files.revize.com/westbend/municipal%20code/09%20Chapter%20Municipal%20Code.pdf

Coops are accessory structures under Chapter 17. Coops and runs must be in rear yards with a minimum 5-foot setback, or in one side yard only with an approved, screened site plan. No coop or run may be within 25 feet of any separate residential or business structure on an adjacent lot. Source: https://cms9files.revize.com/westbend/municipal%20code/09%20Chapter%20Municipal%20Code.pdf

Run enclosures may use welded wire or chicken wire but may not be part of a residential fence on the property. The building-requirements packet also states a maximum accessory-building area of 720 square feet (combined) and a maximum height of 18 feet. Sources: https://cms9files.revize.com/westbendwi/finance/CHICKEN%20PACKET.pdf and https://cms9files.revize.com/westbend/municipal%20code/09%20Chapter%20Municipal%20Code.pdf

summary: City of Baraboo allows up to 6 chickens in the R-1, R-1A, R-2, R-3, and MH-S residential districts with a City Clerk chicken permit. Roosters and crowing cockerels are prohibited. The official fee schedule lists a $30 initial fee and a $20 renewal. Slaughter is prohibited in residential zoning districts.
chickenLimit: Up to 6 chickens per parcel (Sec. 29.13)
roosterRule: Roosters and crowing cockerels shall not be kept (Sec. 29.13)
permitRequired: City Clerk chicken permit required (Sec. 29.13). The City's official fee schedule lists an initial fee of $30 and a renewal of $20. Permits expire on June 30 of every odd-numbered year.
prerequisites: Apply to the City Clerk. On a new (non-renewal) application, the Clerk mails notice to all contiguous property owners, who have 10 business days to file a written objection. If someone objects, the Administrative Committee hears the application; if no objection is filed, the Clerk may issue the permit if inspection and other conditions are met.
The coop and run must be inspected by the City humane officer or designee. The applicant must have no animal-cruelty convictions and may not be delinquent on taxes, assessments, or city claims.

The lot must be at least 50 feet wide and contain only a single-family dwelling (or be an educational setting). All contiguous properties must contain only a single-family or two-family dwelling, with a school-district exception. A zero-lot-line duplex is not eligible.
Current permit holders may apply to renew no sooner than three months, and no later than five days, before expiration; a renewal inspection is required.
rules: Except as allowed in agricultural districts or elsewhere in Chapter 29 (including the chicken permit in Sec. 29.13), Sec. 29.20 prohibits keeping poultry, pigeons, or fowl in any zoning district. Source: https://baraboowi.gov/uploads/dm/9020/CHAPTER_29__ANIMALS

Coops and runs must be at least 10 feet from any lot line and may not be located closer to a neighboring residence than to the residence on the coop's parcel. Source: https://baraboowi.gov/uploads/dm/9020/CHAPTER_29__ANIMALS

A covered coop is required with not less than 2 and not more than 4 square feet per chicken, built of sturdy predator-proof material, with a floor covered in wood or cedar chips. The coop may be built as part of a yard shed or garage but cannot be placed on top of a building. Source: https://baraboowi.gov/uploads/dm/9020/CHAPTER_29__ANIMALS

A predator-proof wire run must be attached to or surround the coop. Chickens must stay in the covered coop or fenced run at all times. Fencing must be tall enough, covered, or the birds' wings clipped to prevent escape. Source: https://baraboowi.gov/uploads/dm/9020/CHAPTER_29__ANIMALS
Slaughtering of chickens in the residential zoning districts is prohibited. Source: https://baraboowi.gov/uploads/dm/9020/CHAPTER_29__ANIMALS

summary: City of Brookfield allows poultry only on R-1 lots of at least 3 acres, at not more than 20 fowl per acre, and only when the birds are confined or enclosed. Keeping poultry on a smaller lot is not allowed under this R-1 standard. There is no backyard-chicken permit program for typical residential lots.
chickenLimit: In the R-1 District, poultry is allowed only on lots of at least 3 acres, at not more than 20 fowl per acre (Sec. 17.28.010(C)). Typical lots under 3 acres are not eligible under this standard.
roosterRule: The R-1 poultry standard does not separately ban or allow roosters; it regulates poultry and fowl, which must be kept confined or enclosed and not permitted to run at large (Sec. 17.28.010(C)). Chapter 6.04 also prohibits animals and fowl from running at large.
permitRequired: No chicken-specific license or permit was found in Chapter 6.04 (Animals Generally) or in R-1 Sec. 17.28.010.
prerequisites: Confirm the property is in the R-1 Residence District and is at least 3 acres. Other residential districts were not fully reviewed section-by-section; do not assume poultry is allowed on a smaller lot in another district.
Check deed restrictions, HOA rules, and any later ordinances not reflected in the opened code sections.
rules: Poultry is restricted, not a general backyard-chicken program. Typical lots under 3 acres are not allowed to keep poultry under Sec. 17.28.010(C). The R-1 standard allows poultry only on lots of at least 3 acres, at not more than 20 fowl per acre, and only if the fowl stay confined or enclosed and are not permitted to run at large. Source: https://ecode360.com/51300592

Brookfield Zoning Code Sec. 17.28.010(C) (R-1 permitted uses) allows keeping of poultry and domestic livestock (including horses, but not hogs, goats, or fur-bearing animals), provided not more than one head of such livestock or more than 20 fowl are kept for each acre of lot area; provided the keeping of poultry or domestic livestock shall not be permitted on any lot less than three acres in area; and provided such fowl are kept confined or enclosed and not permitted to run at large. Source: https://ecode360.com/51300592

Chapter 6.04.010 separately provides that no person having possession or control of any animal or fowl shall allow it to run at large within the city. Source: https://www.codepublishing.com/WI/Brookfield/html/Brookfield06/Brookfield0604.html

summary: Village of McFarland allows up to 4 hens on single-family or two-family dwellings in the R-1, R-1A, R-1B, R-2, and R-3 districts with an annual chicken permit. Roosters are prohibited, and outdoor slaughter is prohibited. The Village permit-forms page links a Chicken Permit Application that says the ordinance was amended on December 9, 2025, and lists a $30 annual fee plus a $50 building permit for a new coop. An older application is still posted and lists a $20 annual fee. It says the ordinance was amended on December 11, 2017 only. Prefer the newer $30 form unless the Village confirms otherwise.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 hens (Sec. 62-69(d))
permitRequired: Annual chicken permit required (Sec. 62-69(d)(8)). The current application (amended December 9, 2025) lists $30 for a new or on-time renewal permit, $60 if renewed after May 31, and a $50 building permit for a new coop. An older application still posted by the Village lists $20 for a new or on-time renewal and $40 after May 31. Prefer the $30 form unless the Village confirms otherwise. The permit year runs June 1 to May 31.
prerequisites: Obtain the annual permit prior to June 1, or within 30 days of acquiring chickens.

Submit Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration, and if renting, a signed owner-approval letter. New applicants also need a building-permit application and a site plan showing the coop, fencing, and distances to property lines and buildings.
The Building Inspector inspects the property for the initial permit; annual renewal does not require re-inspection.
Confirm neighborhood covenants allow chickens, including a letter of approval if needed.
rules: Keeping of no more than four chickens is allowed only in the R-1, R-1A, R-1B, R-2, and R-3 districts, and only where the principal use is a single-family or two-family dwelling (Sec. 62-69(d)). Source: https://www.mcfarland.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/3737/Chicken-Permit-Application-PDF
No person shall keep any roosters. No person shall slaughter chickens outdoors. Source: https://www.mcfarland.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/3737/Chicken-Permit-Application-PDF

Chickens must have a hen house and a fenced outdoor enclosure and must stay in the hen house or enclosure at all times. The hen house must be a covered, predator-resistant, well-ventilated structure providing at least 2 square feet per chicken. Source: https://www.mcfarland.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/3737/Chicken-Permit-Application-PDF

The hen house or outdoor enclosure must be in the rear yard, no closer than 25 feet to any residential dwelling on an adjacent lot, and no closer than 10 feet to the property line. Lot-coverage and height limits for accessory buildings in Sec. 62-227 also apply. Source: https://www.mcfarland.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/3737/Chicken-Permit-Application-PDF

Outdoor feed must be in rat-proof containers. The Zoning Administrator may revoke a permit after two or more violations of this section or Chapter 20 within any six-month period. Failure to obtain the permit can result in doubling the permit fee. Source: https://www.mcfarland.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/3737/Chicken-Permit-Application-PDF

Official village documents disagree on the fee. The application amended December 9, 2025 lists $30 for a new or on-time renewal, $60 after May 31, and a $50 building permit for a new coop. The older application still posted by the Village, amended December 11, 2017 only, lists $20 for a new or on-time renewal and $40 after May 31. Prefer the newer $30 form unless the Village confirms otherwise. Sources: https://www.mcfarland.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/3737/Chicken-Permit-Application-PDF and https://www.mcfarland.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/149/Chicken-Permit-Application-PDF

summary: Village of Oregon, Wisconsin allows accessory poultry keeping of chickens or quail, and ducks on lots of at least 14,500 square feet, with a maximum of 10 birds per property (chicks under 8 weeks do not count). Roosters are prohibited except for documented agricultural-show or academic purposes. Ordinance 25-03 does not create a village chicken license; DATCP registration is required. Slaughter is not addressed in the ordinance text that was opened.
chickenLimit: Up to 10 birds per property (chickens or quail; ducks allowed only on lots of at least 14,500 sq ft). Birds under 8 weeks old do not count toward the limit. Institutional land uses may keep up to 20 birds (Sec. 17-206(8)(aa)).
roosterRule: Roosters prohibited unless the owner provides documentation that the rooster is kept for agricultural show or academic purposes. Roosters count toward the 10-bird limit and are subject to the Village noise ordinance (Sec. 17-206(8)(aa)(1)(c)).
permitRequired: No village poultry-keeping license is created in Ordinance 25-03. All properties keeping poultry must be licensed or registered with the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection. A building permit is required for coops larger than 150 square feet, and an electrical permit is required for permanent electrical work.
prerequisites: Register or license the premises with Wisconsin DATCP before keeping poultry.
Obtain a building permit if the coop will be larger than 150 square feet, and an electrical permit for any permanent electrical work.
Confirm the use is permitted in the property's zoning district under the amended Table of Land Uses in Sec. 17-203 (as amended by Ordinance 25-03, adopted April 21, 2025).
rules: Accessory Poultry Keeping is created as Sec. 17-206(8)(aa) by Village Ordinance 25-03, adopted April 21, 2025 (Plan Commission hearing April 3, 2025; Board vote 6-1). Source: https://www.vil.oregon.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/1209/Ordinance-No-25-03---Poultry--Beekeeping
Geese, swans, peacocks, and other species not listed in the section are prohibited. Source: https://www.vil.oregon.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/1209/Ordinance-No-25-03---Poultry--Beekeeping

Poultry must have access to a structurally sound covered coop, maintained in good repair and kept free from rodents and vermin, and must be enclosed in a fenced yard or run sufficient to contain a chicken. Source: https://www.vil.oregon.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/1209/Ordinance-No-25-03---Poultry--Beekeeping

The coop and run must be in the rear or side yard and are treated as accessory buildings under Sec. 17-015, so they must meet the setback, size, and height requirements of the applicable zoning district. Coops are not allowed in front yards, but may be in a street side yard if behind a permitted fence or within a fenced run set back from the property line at least the height of the fence. Source: https://www.vil.oregon.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/1209/Ordinance-No-25-03---Poultry--Beekeeping

Coops and runs must be clean, dry, and odor-free. Stored feed must be indoors or in a secured enclosed container. Ordinance 25-03 does not state a slaughter rule. Source: https://www.vil.oregon.wi.us/DocumentCenter/View/1209/Ordinance-No-25-03---Poultry--Beekeeping

summary: City of Wisconsin Rapids allows up to 4 hens on lots of one-half acre or less, and up to 8 hens on larger lots, at single-family or two-family residences. Roosters, on-site slaughter, and egg sales are prohibited. The city does not issue a chicken-keeping permit, but DATCP livestock premises registration is required, and a building/accessory permit is required for a coop.
chickenLimit: Up to 4 chickens on lots of 1/2 acre or less; up to 8 chickens on lots more than 1/2 acre. Newborn chicks up to 3 weeks of age may also be kept in a residence or outbuilding (Sec. 25.02(3)(b)(6)).
roosterRule: Roosters prohibited (Sec. 25.02(3)(f)(2)). The ordinance defines chicken as a female hen of any age.
permitRequired: No city permit is required to keep chickens, per the official city Chickens page. Proof of Wisconsin DATCP Livestock Premises Registration is required before keeping chickens (Sec. 25.02(3)(d)(5)). Sec. 25.02(3)(e)(1) requires a building permit for any new coop and enclosure; the city page says an accessory permit is required for large chicken coops.
prerequisites: Register the premises with Wisconsin DATCP before keeping chickens and keep the registration number.
If the property is a rental used as a single-family or two-family residence, obtain written landlord approval and provide it to the Community Development Department.
Submit a drawing of the coop and any attached enclosure with a building permit application for a new coop or enclosure.
rules: Chickens may be kept on a lot used as a single-family or two-family residence, and at educational facilities for educational purposes. They are not allowed in mobile home parks or condominiums, or on a vacant lot unless the keeper lives on the abutting property (Sec. 25.02(3)). Source: https://www.wirapids.gov/DocumentCenter/View/290/Chapter-25-Offenses-Against-Public-PDF

The coop and any attached enclosure must be in the backyard, must meet accessory-building setbacks, and must be at least 25 feet from a residential dwelling on an adjacent lot. Source: https://www.wirapids.gov/DocumentCenter/View/290/Chapter-25-Offenses-Against-Public-PDF

Chickens must stay in a ventilated, roofed coop or attached enclosure at all times. The coop floor must allow at least 4 square feet per chicken, and coop height may not exceed 6 feet. The coop must include clear open space so chickens can walk on the ground or a concrete slab. Enclosures must be built so chickens cannot escape; wire netting may be used only for the coop/enclosure, not as a boundary fence. Source: https://www.wirapids.gov/DocumentCenter/View/290/Chapter-25-Offenses-Against-Public-PDF

Egg sales are prohibited. Slaughter of chickens on the premises is prohibited. Feed and clean water must be available at all times; feed must be stored so rodents and predators cannot reach it. Source: https://www.wirapids.gov/DocumentCenter/View/290/Chapter-25-Offenses-Against-Public-PDF

The city may prohibit keeping chickens on a property after 3 or more violations in 6 months, or 4 or more in 12 months. Source: https://www.wirapids.gov/DocumentCenter/View/290/Chapter-25-Offenses-Against-Public-PDF

The code and the city page do not use the same words for coop permits. Sec. 25.02(3)(e)(1) requires a building permit for any new coop and enclosure. The city Chickens page says no chicken-keeping permit is required and that an accessory permit is required for large chicken coops. Confirm which permit applies with Community Development. Sources: https://www.wirapids.gov/DocumentCenter/View/290/Chapter-25-Offenses-Against-Public-PDF and https://www.wirapids.gov/507/Chickens

summary: City of Davenport allows up to 6 hens on a single-family dwelling with an urban chicken permit. Roosters are prohibited, and slaughter is allowed only at legally operating poultry production facilities. The official payment form lists a $25 non-refundable permit fee. Applicants must complete an approved urban-chicken class and meet coop setbacks of 10 feet from property lines and 25 feet from dwellings.
chickenLimit: Up to 6 female chickens (hens) per tract of land (Sec. 6.06.030)
permitRequired: Urban chicken permit required (Sec. 6.06.021). The official city payment form lists a $25.00 non-refundable permit fee. Fees are otherwise set by City Council resolution (Sec. 6.06.023).
prerequisites: The tract may contain only one single-family dwelling occupied and used as such by the permittee. If the occupant is not the owner, the owner must give permission and is a joint permittee.

Successfully complete an approved class in raising chickens in an urban setting and submit a certificate of completion. The city payment form currently recommends the Iowa State University Extension webinar (the form notes a $25 class fee charged by the Extension, separate from the city permit fee).
Submit a legible site plan showing the coop or tractor location. A new license must be applied for if the permittee relocates.
All amounts owed to the city, including liens, fines, and judgments, must be paid in full.
rules: Chapter 6.06 (Urban Chickens) is the controlling ordinance (eCode360). Source: https://ecode360.com/35584371

Chickens must be kept in an enclosure or fenced area at all times, secured in a henhouse or chicken tractor during non-daylight hours, and may not be in the front yard at any time. Source: https://ecode360.com/35584371

Henhouses must provide at least 4 square feet per bird, be enclosed on all sides with a roof and lockable doors, and be impermeable to rodents, wild birds, and predators. They must be in the rear yard unless setbacks cannot be met, in which case a side yard within the required setbacks is allowed. Source: https://ecode360.com/35584371

Henhouses, chicken runs, and chicken tractors must be at least 10 feet from the property line and at least 25 feet from any principal structure, and must also meet zoning accessory-structure rules. The city's setback graphic shows a 25-foot setback from both the applicant's dwelling and adjacent dwellings, and 10 feet from side and rear property lines. Sources: https://ecode360.com/35584371 and https://www.davenportiowa.com/common/pages/DisplayFile.aspx?itemId=20379867

It is unlawful to slaughter any chickens within the City of Davenport outside of legally operating poultry production facilities (Sec. 6.06.120(D)). Chickens may not be kept inside a dwelling or on a vacant or uninhabited tract. Source: https://ecode360.com/35584371
Stored manure must be in a fully enclosed roofed or lidded structure, and no more than 3 cubic feet of manure may be stored on the tract. Source: https://ecode360.com/35584371

summary: A City of Woodbury ordinance adopted October 23, 2024, allows chicken-hens in the R-1 and R-2 zoning districts (up to 6 hens on lots of 3.99 acres or less, and 2 hens per acre on lots of 4 acres or more), with coops in the rear yard, 20 feet from property lines and 50 feet from adjacent dwellings. Roosters are treated as livestock. A later Ordinance 2085, adopted October 21, 2026, amends the same chapters and, per the official published summary, requires a permit in the R-4 Urban Residential district; the full 2085 text was not opened.
chickenLimit: Under the October 23, 2024 ordinance: up to 6 chicken-hens on 3.99 acres or less, and 2 chicken-hens per acre on 4 acres or more, in the R-1 and R-2 districts (Sec. 5-17 as amended). Ordinance 2085 (adopted October 21, 2026) may have changed where and how many hens are allowed; the full text was not opened.
roosterRule: Under the October 23, 2024 ordinance, roosters are viewed as livestock. Livestock (other than chicken-hens) is allowed on properties zoned for agricultural use of at least 5 acres; more than one livestock animal per acre requires a conditional use permit. Confirm whether Ordinance 2085 changed this.
permitRequired: The October 23, 2024 ordinance text that was opened does not create a chicken permit for R-1/R-2. The official published summary of Ordinance 2085 (adopted October 21, 2026) states that a required permit applies to properties zoned R-4 Urban Residential and that the permit is renewed biennially. The full 2085 text, including fees and when permits become available, was not opened.
prerequisites: Confirm current zoning (especially R-1, R-2, or R-4) and re-check Ordinance 2085 at Woodbury City Hall or an updated code posting before relying on the 2024 limits alone.
Chickens must be kept in a chicken coop and may not run at large. They are not permitted in any portion of the home, garage, and/or accessory building (2024 Sec. 5-17 amendment).
rules: The opened October 23, 2024 ordinance amends Chapter 5, Sec. 5-17, and Chapter 24, adding Sec. 24-285 Chicken Coops. Source: https://mcclibraryfunctions.azurewebsites.us/api/ordinanceDownload/14365/1324633/pdf

Under that 2024 text, one chicken coop is allowed per principal dwelling in R-1 and R-2. The coop must be in the rear yard, outside easements, at least 50 feet from adjacent dwellings and 20 feet from all property lines, no more than 50 square feet (measured at the exterior perimeter), and no more than 7 feet high. Source: https://mcclibraryfunctions.azurewebsites.us/api/ordinanceDownload/14365/1324633/pdf

Non-rigid materials such as poultry netting must be framed with rigid materials and kept taut and in good repair. The coop must be maintained as to materials and sanitation. Source: https://mcclibraryfunctions.azurewebsites.us/api/ordinanceDownload/14365/1324633/pdf

A chicken coop is not viewed as an accessory building. Chicken runs attached to, or within 5 feet of, a structure housing chickens are viewed as part of the chicken coop. Source: https://mcclibraryfunctions.azurewebsites.us/api/ordinanceDownload/14365/1324633/pdf

Ordinance 2085, adopted October 21, 2026, changes R-4 permits. Only the 2024 R-1 and R-2 rules are fully verified. The official published summary says Ordinance 2085 allows chickens on single-family detached residentially zoned properties, requires a permit for all properties zoned R-4 Urban Residential, sets performance standards for coops and runs, provides for biennial permit renewal, and identifies discontinued-use and removal standards. The full 2085 text was not opened, so those 2026 details are not treated as verified numeric rules. Sources: https://marketplace.twincities.com/st-paul/legals-public-notices/city-of-woodbury-summary-of-ordinance-no.-2085/AC1E03BF1914627123cZ9c19F9C3 and https://mcclibraryfunctions.azurewebsites.us/api/ordinanceDownload/14365/1324633/pdf
